- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.3) — model tends to overshoot in bullish phases.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (especially < -0.4) — model fails to capture downside risk or mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag in downward trends — true prices often dip faster than model predicts.
- After sharp price spikes, model overreacts and forecasts a prolonged upward trend — correct by reducing slope after peak.
- Mean reversion bias: model holds prices too high in consolidation or after strong rallies — adjust downward by 5–10% of recent peak if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overweights recent volatility — dampen forecast if sentiment is low or trending sideways.
- If sentiment turns sharply negative mid-period, reduce forecast slope aggressively — avoid “sustained rally” bias.
- Model underestimates downside risk in low-sentiment periods — add 2–5% buffer below forecast if sentiment < -0.3 for 3+ days.
